source_snapshot.test_name_items: All SAS/SATA NVMe LED Check - Raid fail
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check if NVMe RAID fail LED function works normally

1. Insert NVMe SSD into BP slot and create RAID 1
2. Unplug one NVMe SSD from RAID group
3. Check RAID fail LED

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. Check system spec define LED function

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: Undocumented raw IPMI bytes plus `lsblk` inventory.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: Management result, device list and physical Fail LED observation.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL; omits RAID creation/member removal and transport resolution, and proposes unverified raw BMC control.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED; adds transport decision, disposable targets, degraded evidence, physical fault and recovery ownership.

original_test_intent: Create an isolated RAID 1, remove one member and observe the physical RAID-fail indicator across an intended drive population, but the master source conflicts between SAS/SATA scope and an explicitly NVMe procedure.
original_method: Retain separate SAS/SATA and NVMe failure plans pending owner resolution; each needs its own controller, disposable members, enclosure/bay mapping, RAID implementation and Fail LED truth table. Neither may be inferred from the other.
manual_activity: The eventual test requires a human member unplug and visual Fail LED observation, but even these cannot be safely defined until the controller/transport conflict is resolved.
required_inputs: Selected controller/RAID support and disposable member serials
Stable enclosure/bay/member map and safe removal procedure
Fail LED color/pattern/timing and degraded-state criterion
Backup/OOB, post-fault disposition and rebuild/recovery ownership
safety_requirements: Do not create an array or remove a member while transport/controller/targets are ambiguous.
Exclude boot, mounted, protected, data-bearing and unknown drives.
Verify healthy synchronized RAID 1 and exact member/bay before human removal.
Do not send undocumented raw IPMI bytes or use inventory as failure proof.
No automatic retry, reinsertion, rebuild, deletion or initialization.
agent_execution_scope: Preserve the transport conflict and prepare distinct safe plans.
After resolution, validate destructive scope and automate approved RAID build/telemetry only.
Correlate degraded events with operator physical evidence.
Do not claim physical action, LED result or verdict.
engineer_actions: Resolve transport and approve disposable members, fault and recovery plan.
Physically remove the exact member and visually record the Fail LED.
Authorize recovery separately and issue PASS/FAIL.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Non-equivalent and unsafe: raw bytes/lsblk neither choose transport nor create RAID 1/member failure, and provide no validated LED target.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Perform no state change before scope resolution; then use selected controller-native RAID build/read-only degraded telemetry with manual fault/visual proof.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: SAS/SATA label, NVMe RAID 1/removal procedure, Fail LED criterion and 15/8-minute fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: After resolution, use a signed member/bay/array manifest, healthy baseline, synchronized removal/degraded events and operator Fail LED video.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Selected SAS/SATA or NVMe RAID path.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record controller/backplane/BMC firmware, driver and utility versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Selected controller degraded-array and platform Fail LED/hot-remove documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Separates incompatible fault paths and adds recovery gates.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Wrong-path array creation can erase data before any useful LED evidence exists.

project_override_considerations: A documented project override may choose one transport/population; it cannot claim the unselected hardware family or omitted member/bay coverage.
expected_evidence: Owner decision, selected topology/LED spec and destructive approval
Healthy RAID 1 build/sync evidence and exact member map
Operator removal/LED media plus matching degraded controller/OS/BMC events
Post-state/recovery, Tool Result and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Test Set/item specify SAS/SATA while the procedure explicitly uses NVMe SSDs. RAID implementation, controller, member addressing and LED path are transport-specific.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Choosing hardware or destructive targets before transport resolution is unsafe and may test the wrong function. This is genuine semantic blocking.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects its raw/inventory shortcut as omitting the destructive physical failure path.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Adopts transport and target safeguards, tightening classification to BLOCKED until resolved.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Prevents approval/package readiness from concealing a true hardware-scope conflict.

review_improvement: Stops destructive RAID creation on an inferred transport and preserves the real physical failure requirement.
independent_technical_reasoning: RAID 1 creation and member removal are high-consequence and controller-specific. A SAS/SATA label cannot safely be reconciled with an NVMe procedure without authoritative owner input.
no_automatic_retry: No array, physical or management operation is permitted before transport resolution.
